svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The loop of Henle: a countercurrent multiplier."], [1, "The thick ascending limb pumps Na\u207a and Cl\u207b out into the medulla; it is impermeable to water."], [4, "This makes the medulla salty, increasingly so deeper down."], [6.5, "In the descending limb water leaves by osmosis, so the filtrate becomes concentrated (up to about 1200)."], [9.5, "Going up, salt is removed and the filtrate leaves the loop dilute (about 100)."], [12, "With ADH, water leaves the collecting duct into the salty medulla: concentrated urine."]]
svg.title: The loop of Henle
svg.desc: The loop of Henle as a countercurrent multiplier: the ascending limb pumps sodium and chloride ions into the medulla, water leaves the descending limb by osmosis, and the collecting duct loses water when ADH is present; solute concentrations in mOsm/kg shown.
svg.text: The loop of Henle: countercurrent multiplier
Numbers are solute concentrations in mOsm/kg (human values, approximate).

g.data-info: Solute concentration rises from about 300 mOsm/kg in the cortex to about 1200 deep in the human medulla. Longer loops make steeper gradients (e.g. desert rodents).
Impermeable to water. Actively pumps Na⁺ and Cl⁻ out into the medulla (using ATP), so the filtrate becomes dilute as it goes up.
Permeable to water but not to salt: water leaves by osmosis into the salty medulla, so the filtrate becomes more concentrated as it goes down.
Fluid flows down one limb and up the other, in opposite directions: this multiplies the effect of the salt pumping into a large gradient.
Passes down through the salty medulla. With ADH, aquaporins open and water leaves by osmosis: concentrated urine.
Capillaries that loop alongside, removing reabsorbed water without washing the gradient away (countercurrent exchange).

g.text: ascending limb: salt out, no water
descending limb: water out, no salt
